title: Your Fund Lost 15% — IRS Still Wants $3,200
hook: Your mutual fund lost money last year. Then the IRS sent you a tax bill. Here's the legal trick fund companies use to dump taxes on you.
angle: Mutual fund capital gains distributions: fund managers' trades inside the fund create taxable events that get passed to shareholders — even when the fund loses value. ETFs are immune. Most investors have no idea this exists.
audience: Brokerage account holders with actively managed mutual funds (not in an IRA); anyone surprised by a 1099-DIV capital gains distribution
key_numbers: Average 2022 mutual fund distribution: 8.3% of NAV
$8,300 in phantom taxable income on a $100K portfolio
70% of actively managed funds distributed capital gains in down years
Americans paid ~$14 billion in unnecessary mutual fund taxes
